item.title: Cost of Living in Point Cook Melbourne
item.description:
Money stretches differently in every suburb. In Point Cook, here is exactly how far your dollar goes.

Read our full Point Cook suburb guide for the bigger picture.

Is Point Cook Expensive?

Point Cook sits somewhere in the middle of Melbourne’s cost spectrum. It’s not cheap, but it’s not going to break the bank either — assuming you’re realistic about expectations.

The cost of living here reflects what the suburb offers. Location, community, access to amenities — you get what you pay for, and in Point Cook, you’re generally getting good value for the price point.

item.title: Getting Around Point Cook — Transport Guide
item.description:
Two words define transport in Point Cook: train-dependent. Everything else is detail.

Check out our full Point Cook suburb guide for the complete picture.

Getting Around Point Cook — The Quick Version

Public transport in Point Cook is decent. You can get to the city in roughly 30 to 50 minutes during peak hours. Having a car helps, especially for weekend errands and trips outside the PT network.

Train Access

Point Cook is served by train, though you may need to get to the nearest station which can be a short walk or bus ride away.

item.title: Point Cook — History and How It's Changed
item.description:
The history of Point Cook is not just dates and facts - it is the DNA of the current personality of this suburb.

See our full Point Cook suburb guide for the current picture.

What Point Cook Was Originally

Before it was what you see today, Point Cook was agricultural land and market gardens. The original residents built the suburb’s foundation — the street grid, the housing stock, the community institutions that still exist in some form.

item.title: Point Cook Neighbourhood Guide — Streets and Pockets
item.description:
Point Cook isn’t one monolithic block. Like most Melbourne suburbs, it has different pockets with different personalities. Here’s how to read the suburb from the inside.

See our full Point Cook suburb guide for the overview.

Point Cook Isn’t Just One Thing

Walk from one end of Point Cook to the other and you’ll notice the vibe shift. The main commercial strip has one energy. The residential streets behind it have another. And the edges of the suburb — where it bleeds into Altona Meadows — have their own thing going on.
